summary: Upgraded the ClientApp from Angular 8.1 to Angular 9.1 using `ng update @angular/core@9 @angular/cli@9`, which also bumped TypeScript to 3.8, zone.js to 0.10 and rxjs to 6.6 and applied Angular's own v9 migrations (Ivy/AOT flags in angular.json, tsconfig files/include rewrites, server render re-exports in main.ts). @ngrx/* was bumped from 8.6.1 to 9.2.1 via `ng update` because ngrx 8 only peers on @angular/core ^8. install and build pass; the unit tests still fail for the same pre-existing angular.json misconfiguration that made them fail at baseline.
changes: angular.json: build options gained `"aot": true` and the production config gained an `anyComponentStyle` budget (Angular v9 CLI migration).
src/tsconfig.app.json and src/tsconfig.server.json: `exclude` replaced with explicit `files`/`include` entries (Angular v9 migration).
src/main.ts: Angular's v9 migration appended `export { renderModule, renderModuleFactory } from '@angular/platform-server';` for the Universal server build.
@ngrx migration schematics 'The road to v9' ran for @ngrx/effects and @ngrx/router-store; they reported no source changes needed.
package.json and package-lock.json updated together through npm/ng update, so the lockfile is in sync.
No application source logic was changed; behaviour is unchanged.
manual_followups: Unit tests still fail (as at baseline): angular.json's test target lists `"styles": ["styles.css"]` instead of `"src/styles.css"`, so webpack cannot resolve the entry and karma never runs a spec. This path was already wrong before the upgrade and was left untouched to keep the hop minimal; fixing it is a one-line change that would let the suite actually execute.

`@nguniversal/module-map-ngfactory-loader` is still pinned at 7.1.0 and emits an Angular 7 peer warning. It is deprecated from Angular 9 onward (Ivy makes it unnecessary); the SSR entry `src/app/app.server.module.ts` still imports `ModuleMapLoaderModule`. The browser build is unaffected, but `npm run build:ssr` was not part of the required checks and was not verified.

Ivy is enabled by default in Angular 9 (`aot: true` was added to the build options). A manual smoke test of the running app is worth doing, since Ivy can surface runtime differences that a successful compile does not catch.

The optional dependency `node-sass@4.11.0` fails to compile on Node 12 in this environment (node-gyp cannot find a Python 2). It is optional so `npm install` still succeeds, exactly as at baseline, but it should be replaced with `sass` in a later hop.
